recipes.name: Tater Tot Bake
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef with the onions. Drain excess fat, and season with salt and pepper to taste.

Spread the beef mixture evenly over the bottom of a 2 quart casserole dish. Arrange tater tots evenly over beef layer. In a small bowl, stir the soup into the milk until smooth; pour over tater tot and beef layers. Sprinkle Cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake in preheated oven for 30 to 40 minutes, until cheese is bubbly and slightly brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Tater Tot Bake
raw_recipe.description: A lickety-split version of that ever-popular standby, shepherd's pie. Seasoned ground beef and onions are sauteed, layered in a casserole with potatoes, topped with condensed cream of mushroom soup, sprinkled with cheese and baked.

review.reviewBody:
After reading the reviews, I used this recipe as a jumping off point and made the following changes: Used 2lbs of ground sirloin, 1 can cream of mushroom, 1 can cheddar cheese soup, a full bag of tater tots, and a can of french style green beans. I browned the beef with the onion and a teaspoon of minced garlic, and 1 tablespoon greek seasoning. I then mixed the soups and 1 cup of milk into the meat after it was browned and drained. I layered the greenbeans on the bottom of a 9X13 casserole dish, spooned the meat mixture over it, then sprinkled 2 cups of shredded cheddar over that, then topped with the tots, which I patted down into the cheese. sprinkled the whole thing with some fresh ground pepper, and baked at 350 for 40 minutes. 
For those other reviewers who complained about blandness, well I think it's common sense to season your meat while cooking, and hey, be adventurous and use this recipe as a starting point, tweak it with different soups, cheeses, spices...My family and I really enjoyed this dish, and while I did make changes, I think this recipe deserves 5 stars for a great basic recipe, and inspiration. I am looking forward to the leftovers for lunch tomorrow, I am betting that like most casseroles like this, it'll taste even better tomorrow! :)

I enjoyed this. 

Tablespoon sour cream to soup mixture, season meat well, fresh onion and garlic to meat, line bottom with can of corn drained. Layer corn, meat, cheese, soup mixture, tator tots, more cheese. Cook 40 minutes. Broil briefly.

I cooked the ground beef with salt, pepper, granulated garlic and Italian seasoning. Then, I added the chopped onion and cooked them until tender. To that, I added half of a can of Del Monte whole kernel corn, drained. I blended cream of celery soup and 3/4 cup of milk in a saucepan and poured it over the meat mixture in an 8x8 casserole. Next, I added 4 handfuls of Mexican cheese blend, put the tots on next, and added a thin layer of shredded cheese. I topped it with 1/2 tsp. of smoked sweets paprika. 35 minutes at 350, then 20 minutes at 300.Good luck and happy eating

I made this a one pan dish by using my cast-iron skillet. I sautéed the beef and onion. Then I added the premixed milk and soup to the beef and mixed it all together. Next, I added a can of drained green beans on top followed by 2 cups of cheese. I topped it with hash browns. I baked it at 400° for 40 minutes.

I added thawed frozen veggies and the tater tots I used had a seasoning on them already. I also cooked the meat in a cast iron pan. That way, after I drained the grease off, I was able to pop the whole thing in the oven and have one less dish to clean.

My parents enjoyed it. It was super easy to make and clean up

Turned out very good! I too added the soup to the meat (pork sausage) and also I embedded the tater tots into the mixture somewhat. Also placed under the broiler for a couple minutes to crisp up the top to a golden brown! Very good. You could also add some veggies to get some nutrition into the kids!

This is a good recipe. After reading some reviews I developed my plan. I sautéed my onion with some finely chopped carrots and celery, then browned my ground beef (about 1 and1/3 lb) along with the vegetables; seasoning that beef with salt, and garlic pepper and a tiny dash of cayenne. I had about 1/2 cup sour cream in the fridge and added that to the soup mixture and mixed it with the ground beef mixture; then threw in some frozen green peas and at least a cup of the cheddar. I let the tater tots thaw after I added them to the top, then sprinkled another 1/2 cup of the cheese over all, before baking. This was gobbled up by adults and little kids. We all agreed that the tots were probably best in the crispy state. So basically shepherds pie with tots instead of mash. Again, the pan was clea

Gluten free option: I made this gluten free by using Ore-Ida gluten free tater tots and Pacific (or Imagine brand) gluten free cream of mushroom soup mix found at Whole Foods. I mixed ground turkey and a roll of Jimmy Dean original sausage, which is gluten free and I substituted some garlic salt and onion powder for chopped onions, and mixed soup with cooked meat to layer. I put cheese on top of meet pushing the tater tots into the cheese and then sprinkled some cheese on top of Tatar tots. It was a hit with my husband and 11 year old daughter, although my 8 year old son doesn't care for anything mixed together:-/.

This was a family favourite as the kids were growing up and now it’s a favourite of the grandkids. Because we prefer it I’ve made a couple changes. First one kid won’t eat anything with onions so I skip them but if he’s not there I add onions with the cooking beef. I also don’t dilute the mushroom soup and I layer it all with tater tots on the bottom and end it with tater tots on the top. This makes the tater tots nice and crispy on the top. Try this recipe and your kids will thank you.

My kids liked it, next time i will add some bacon to give it some flavor and possibly add garlic. Also, spreading some cheese on top of beef under the tater tots prior to baking would improve this dish

I've made this quite a few times. It is a bit bland if you do it as stated, but this recipe is so great as a starter and so unforgiving. We use only ground venison, I cook it with diced onions. Season to our taste, lots of garlic powder added, salt and pepper. Cream of mushroom soup with a little bit of milk. Green beans layered on bottom. Add some fresh sliced mushrooms or canned button mushrooms with the meat mix. Then layer of cheddar or mozarella, then the tater tots on top.

This is a great starter recipe, but need to make sure you season well. 😉 I started with ground beef, didn't drain, 85/15 beef, used 1.5 lbs, and added onion & carrots, sautéed and then added minced garlic, until fragrant. I then added 1/4 c flour, and cooked for a minute. I then added garlic powder, onion powder and smoked paprika, mixed it up and put in the baking dish. I only had condensed cream of chicken, I added thyme, oregano, a bit more milk and any other dried herbs I had at the ready, (I suggest that you use what you like). Mixed well and poured over tots. As for cheese, I used a combo of what we had. Cheddar, muenster and Colby Jack. I broiled it after 35 minutes and it came out bubbly. Cooled rather quickly and it was a hit. My carb free 21 year old could not resist. My picky eaters ate some, which is better than none, and my husband had 4 helping. The man was off all day and had not eaten cause he can't cook.... but anywho, great starter, will make again, no picture, they ate it all.
I love it! Easy and fun..I put my own spin on it tho...added 1/2 pack of taco seasoning to meat and added three blend cheese and then topped it off with the rest of the taco seasoning!! YUM YUM!!
I used cream of chicken instead of mushroom. And I was low on shredded cheese so I used sliced understand laying over the tater tots. It was delicious and so easy to make, even I could do it!

I remember my mom making this when I was growing up. She made it with tots and cheese on top as another reviewer suggested; however I got in a hurry and ended up making exactly as written. Deliciously either way!
Love the recipe as-is, but the second time I made it I added some sausage with the ground beef and then topped each serving with homemade green chili with pork. Turned out fantastic.
It was good, put some granulated garlic in the hamburger meat and a little pepper.
